info.name: Order & Payment API
info.description:
REST API for orders and payments (Laravel 12, JWT, strategy pattern for payment gateways).

## Quick start
1. Start the API (`php artisan serve`) and set the `base_url` collection variable if it is not `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
2. Run the requests **in order** (or use the Collection Runner): Register -> Login -> Orders -> Payments -> Logout.
3. Tokens and ids are stored in collection variables by the test scripts, so nothing needs to be copied by hand.

Every request has **saved examples** for its success and error responses (400-level cases included).

## Error format
Errors return JSON: `{ "message": "..." }`, plus an `errors` object for validation failures (422).
`401` missing/invalid token - `403` not your resource - `404` not found - `422` validation / business rule.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: Register, login and profile. Run **Register** first: it creates a user and stores its JWT.

request.description:
Creates a user and returns a JWT.

A unique e-mail is generated for every run (pre-request script) so the request can be re-sent safely.

**Rules:** `name` required; `email` required, valid, unique; `password` required, min 6 chars.

Throttled to 10 requests per minute.

response.name: 422 Unprocessable Entity - e-mail already taken
422 Unprocessable Entity - invalid input

request.description:
Authenticates a user and returns a JWT. The token is stored in the `token` collection variable and sent automatically (Bearer) by every other request.

Throttled to 10 requests per minute.

response.name: 422 Unprocessable Entity - missing fields

request.description: Error case: valid e-mail with a wrong password returns **401** and does not change the stored token.
Returns the authenticated user. Requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

item.name: 2. Orders
item.description: Order CRUD. Every endpoint only sees/changes the **authenticated user's own** orders.

request.description:
Creates an order for the authenticated user. The **total is calculated on the server** from the items (quantity x price); the order starts as `pending`. The new id is stored in `order_id`.

**Rules:** `items` required (min 1); each item needs `product_name` (string), `quantity` (integer >= 1), `price` (number >= 0).

response.name: 422 Unprocessable Entity - invalid quantity
422 Unprocessable Entity - empty items

exec: pm.test('Total is calculated by the server', function () { pm.expect(json.data.total_amount).to.eql(1250.5); });

request.description: Paginated list of **the authenticated user's** orders. Enable the `status` query param to filter.

exec: pm.test('Returns data and pagination meta', function () { pm.expect(json.data).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(json.meta.total).to.be.a('number'); });

request.description: Returns one order with its items and payment. Only the owner can view it (**403** otherwise).

response.name: 403 Forbidden - order belongs to another user

request.description: Updates the order status (`pending`, `confirmed`, `cancelled`). Payments can only be processed for **confirmed** orders. Only the owner can update, and a cancelled order can no longer be updated (**403**).

response.name: 403 Forbidden - order belongs to another user
422 Unprocessable Entity - invalid status

request.description: Deletes an order **only if it has no payments** (otherwise **422**). To keep your main order intact, the pre-request script creates a throw-away order and deletes that one.

response.name: 422 Unprocessable Entity - order has payments
403 Forbidden - order belongs to another user

exec: body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ items: [{ product_name: 'Disposable item', quantity: 1, price: 10 }] }) }

item.name: 3. Payments
item.description: Payment processing and history. Gateways are resolved by `payment_method` (see the README to add a new one).

request.description:
Simulates a payment through the gateway chosen by `payment_method` (strategy pattern). Supported: `credit_card`, `paypal`.

**Business rules:** the order must belong to you, be in `confirmed` status, and not be paid already. Run **Update Order (confirm)** first.

response.name: 422 Unprocessable Entity - order is not confirmed
422 Unprocessable Entity - unsupported payment method
422 Unprocessable Entity - order does not exist
403 Forbidden - order belongs to another user

request.description: Error case: paying the same order twice is rejected with **422**.

query.description: Optional: only the payments of this order

request.description: Paginated list of **the authenticated user's** payments. Enable `order_id` to see the payments of one order.

response.name: 200 OK - another user sees only their own (empty)

exec: pm.test('Returns data and pagination meta', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data).to.be.an('array'); });

item.name: 4. Logout
item.description: Kept in its own folder so it runs last.

request.description: Invalidates the current JWT. Run it **last**: the token cannot be used afterwards (**401**).
